why: What I checked: I ran useLine on every unit of 'shooty' and on made-up units. The rule statements come from useSentence and match Select Weapons ('While shooting: You can select one or more ranged weapons that model has'; 'While fighting: You must select one melee weapon') and Close-quarters. useLine's own 'Every model can shoot with one or more of its guns' is only reached when every line's sentence is the plain 'one or both/more' form, so the rules side is fine. The flag is that it claims more than the gear data shows. (1) Can be reached later, not with this list: `const lines = u.gear.map(...).filter(l => l.set.length && own(l.i))` drops models lines that carry none of these weapons. 'every model' is then judged against that shortened list: `others = multi.length < lines.length`, then `if(kind === 'ranged' && !others && ...) 'Every model can shoot with one or more of its guns'`. A models line with no gun therefore doesn't stop 'Every model'. Tested: models ['4× Boy w/ A','4× Boy w/ B','1× Nob'] where the Nob has only a Klaw gives 'Every model can shoot with one or more of its guns.' The same filtered list also drives the unnamed sentence (`kinds.length === 1 && multi.length === lines.length`) and 'One of these per model' (`!multi.length`, `lines.length >= 2`). So both are said for the whole unit (or its part) even when some models line has none. (2) bug, happens in this list: `l.who.replace(/ w\/.*$/, '')` strips the only thing that makes the line different. On Mek + Tankbustas ranged it prints 'Tankbusta can shoot with one or both.' and 'The others: one each'. But 'Tankbusta' is the name of 5 models, and the gear data gives two Busta Rokkit Launchas only to '1× Tankbusta w/ Two Busta Rokkit Launchas'. The other 4× Tankbusta have one. So the sentence reads as if every Tankbusta has two. (3) bug, not reached in this list: `[...new Map(multi.map(l => [key(l), l])).values()]` keeps only the LAST line for each weapon set. An earlier line with the same two-weapon set is not named and ends up implied in 'The others: one each'. Tested: Kaptin and Gitz both [Choppa, Klaw] plus Boyz [Choppa] gives 'Gitz picks one to fight with: Choppa or Klaw. The others: one each'. That says the Kaptin has one weapon when he has two. (4) bug, cannot happen with the current data convention: in the `!multi` branch, `it.carrier = l.who` overwrites, so an item with no n that sits in two lines would name only the last one. The rest is literal: the 'Nob' carrier for Rokkit pistol and Choppa/Smash Hammer (1× line, one copy), the attached-unit split (part 0 = leader line 0), and 'Nob picks one to fight with: Choppa or Smash Hammer'.
fix: Judge 'every model' against all models lines of the part, not only those holding these weapons: `const allLines = u.gear.map((g, i) => i).filter(own); const everyLine = lines.length === allLines.length;`. Give the unnamed useSentence, 'Every model can shoot with one or more of its guns' and 'One of these per model' only when everyLine. Otherwise name each line, and say which models have none of these. Keep the full models-line name (u.models[i] without the count, e.g. 'Tankbusta w/ Two Busta Rokkit Launchas') whenever its ' w/…'-stripped name equals another models line's stripped name in the unit. In `kinds`, group the lines that share a set and name every who in the group (or emit one sentence per line) instead of keeping the last. In the !multi branch, set it.carrier only when the item is in exactly one line.

why: No rule logic here, only checkable list facts: the count per models line, the base from the stat line, the leader or single model marked with name + Warlord/enhancement, and the other lines marked with the wargear they have more of than the most common line. Output for 'shooty' matches the data: Mek+Tankbustas gives Mek; Nob (40mm) · Choppa + Rokkit pistol + Smash Hammer; '2× Busta Rokkit Launcha' for the Tankbusta w/ Two; 4× standard (Busta Rokkit Launcha, Gitstikka). Mek+Flash Gitz gives Mek; Kaptin; 9× standard. Copies are left to screenBases, which multiplies by c: 13× 32mm, 13× 40mm, 30× 25mm all check out. bug, not reached in this list: `more` keeps only gear a line has MORE of (`cnt(l.gear, g) > cnt(std.gear, g)`). A line with the standard's base name whose gear is a subset of the standard, or which lacks one of its items, falls through to `|| 'standard'`. Tested: '1× Boy w/ shiv' with [Slugga] against 4× Boy [Slugga, Choppa] is marked 'standard', though its wargear differs. Note (helper baseOf, not this function): when no stat line matches a models line, it takes the closest-prefix profile. For the Kaptin that is the only bodyguard profile, Flash Gitz 40mm, which is fine here. With no match at all it would still pick a row. Aside (screenBases, not this item): `'(1, 2' + (c > 2 ? ', 3' : '') + ')'` prints '(1, 2, 3)' for 4 or more copies. This list has at most 3.

perBattle reads the count from '(once|twice|three times) per battle' (not 'per battle round'). It is army-wide if the tag or text has 'per battle … per army' or 'one model/unit from your army with this ability'. Otherwise abilityTicks gives one set per copy (copyKey adds .i only when copies > 1). This matches the stated behaviour. Data check: Fix Dat Armour Up and Boss' Ammo Runt 'Once per battle, per unit' give 1 box each. Bomb Squig 'Once per turn, twice per battle, per unit' on Mek+Tankbustas (copies 2) gives 2 boxes × Unit 1/Unit 2. Intimidating Motivation 'Once per battle round, per army' gets no boxes, which is right. The keys match the ones screenPregame's abTicks uses, so a box ticked on the datasheet shows ticked on Pre-game. Abilities with naReason get no boxes. Not reached here: the army-wide test needs the words 'with this ability' after 'one unit from your army', or a 'per army' tag. Text worded 'once per battle, one unit from your army can …' without them would get a set per unit. No ability in this list is worded like that.

It looks the name up: the unit's own ability first (kind = who + tag, else 'datasheet ability'), then ruleFor (army or detachment rule with its src, or a core rule). It returns that rule's own text, with no rule logic. I simulated every grant in the data: Cybork Boosta → 'Enhancement' (M); More Dakka → 'datasheet ability'; Dakka! Dakka! Dakka! → 'Shoota Boyz detachment rule'; Supa-glowy Fing → 'Enhancement'; Kustom Dakka → 'Mek · datasheet ability'; Supa-snazz Dakka → 'Flash Gitz · Upgrade'. Each source text does grant the marked keyword or value without a condition. Kustom Dakka is correctly taken from the Mek's ability ('This unit's ranged attacks have [IGNORES COVER]') and not from the Kustom Dakka stratagem (+1 to wound). Safe on null: when u is undefined it falls back to ruleFor, and an unknown name gives empty text.

The headline is the granting rule(s) (`gs.map(g => g.name).join(' + ')`) with each rule's kind and full text. Then comes the note 'Already in the keywords/value shown (as New Recruit and BSData list them/it)', which is a source attribution, and then the keyword's own rule, smaller. 'Not the 1CP Kustom Dakka stratagem, which has the same name.' is a checkable fact: the stratagem exists in Shoota Boyz and gives +1 to wound, not IGNORES COVER. Rendered for every grant in this list. It adds no conditions and draws no conclusions. Safe on null: the unit is looked up with find and may be undefined, kw may be null, textWithTable/rt accept empty text.

Output for 'shooty' (rendered): everything shown is in the cited rules or is a list fact. Reserves: 'up to 1000 pts (50% of the 2000 limit), counting units embarked within a TRANSPORT you place there' = 20.01 'cannot exceed 50% of your points limit … (including those embarked within TRANSPORTS …)'. 'only arrive from the second battle round onwards … not arrived by the end of round 3 are destroyed (not repositioned units, nor units embarked within a TRANSPORT that arrived)' = 20.03, with 'unless otherwise stated' kept. 'Can Deep Strike' lists Wazdakka 200 and Deffkoptas 85 (all 285), using Deep Strike's 'if every model in this unit has this ability'. Every round: Da Boss ('At the start of the battle round'). Uses per battle: War Cry 1, Fix Dat Armour Up 1, Boss' Ammo Runt 1, Bomb Squig 2 per copy × 2, Insane Bravery 1. Nothing the list has is dropped. The flags are code that would misfile or drop items for other inputs. Neither path is reached by this list. (1) Leaves out a case it names ('start of round 1'): `row('First round', first.map(abLine)...)` checks only abilities. `round` checks rules with `/start of (the|each|every) battle round/`, which does not match 'start of the first battle round'. So an army or detachment rule acting at the start of the first battle round appears in neither row. (2) Lists items where their text can't take effect: `PREGAME_RE` includes `\bdeploy`, which matches 'deployment zone'. Tested: 'In your Movement phase, … more than 9" from the enemy deployment zone' matches, so an in-battle ability would go under 'Deployment and pre-battle abilities'. (3) Abilities whose text names 'read mission objectives' go under the Deployment section, not under 'Read Mission Objectives step' (`early` checks only rules). Minor: the Scouts filter also applies the 'every model' condition to Infiltrators, whose rule text is not in the data, so that condition is unchecked for it. 'Enhance­ments' lists Supa-snazz Dakka, which the data tags 'Upgrade' (u.upgrade). Labelling it an enhancement is not in the source; tag it '(upgrade)' or rename the row. bugs, not reached here: `detachments().find(x => x.enhancements.some(...))` throws if a detachment has no enhancements array. In Transports, `rt(ab.text).replace(/^

|<\/p>$/g, '')` never strips anything, because rt wraps its output in

, so a div ends up inside a span (display only; no transports in this list).
fix:
First round: `row('First round', rulesOf.filter(x => /start of the first battle round/i.test(x.r.text)).map(ruleLine).concat(first.map(abLine)).join('
'))`. Replace `\bdeploy` in PREGAME_RE with step/timing words only, e.g. `deploy armies|deployed (their|your) armies|during deployment|\bredeploy`, so 'deployment zone' alone no longer matches. Read Mission Objectives row: also list `group(allAbs.filter(([u, ab]) => /read mission objectives/i.test(ab.text))).map(abLine)` and leave those out of `pre`. Use `(x.enhancements || [])`. Mark upgrades as such in the Enhancements row.
